scope: Synthetic isolated Chromium DOM observation for repeated EasyWeb source highlighting cleanup. No live third-party pages, classifier or user inputs were involved.

commonSteps: Create a new div with no style attribute and append it to the document.
Set inline outline: 4px solid #087e76 !important and outline-offset: 5px !important through CSSStyleDeclaration.setProperty.
Apply the variant-specific getAttribute read timing around removeAttribute(style).
Read the final style attribute once, then remove the synthetic div.
reproduction.coreBrowserCode: const control = document.createElement('div'); document.body.append(control); control.style.setProperty('outline', '4px solid #087e76', 'important'); control.style.setProperty('outline-offset', '5px', 'important'); control.style.removeProperty('outline'); control.style.removeProperty('outline-offset'); /* Optional: control.getAttribute('style') here, before deletion. */ control.removeAttribute('style'); const result = control.getAttribute('style');

interpretation: In this observed environment, after CSSOM property removal the subsequent attribute read returned an empty style attribute when no read preceded attribute deletion. Reading the serialized style attribute before deletion produced a final null value. This supports synchronizing the serialized style attribute before removing an originally absent empty style attribute in the highlight restore path.
limitations: These are observations from one installed Chromium version and one synthetic DOM sequence.
The experiment does not establish whether the behavior is a browser defect or whether other browser versions behave identically.
The script does not test the full extension, reinjection UI or actual user task completion. Highlight Playwright regression results are recorded separately.
